column1: The chest is lying open, casually spilling its contents onto the floor: YOUR stolen property! Quickly you recover your possessions.
column2: 箱子敞开着，财物随意倾泻于地：正是你被盗之物！你匆忙收回所有家当。

column1: The citizens of $PlaceName are hereby prohibited from travelling about the streets in darkness, after the hour of Compline, unless unavoidably required by their occupation, or by an emergency.
column2: 自今起，禁止$PlaceName市民于晚祷之后在街上游走，除非因职业所需或紧急情况不得不外出。

column1: The city is in a furor. There are mobs in the streets, marching to protest the policies of the $CityLordTitle. Political debates rage everywhere.
column2: 全城骚动。街头群集游行，抗议$CityLordTitle的政策。各地政论纷争不绝。

column1: The city is seething with energy and activity. Rumors are rife about marches on the $VarString1, about taking the city gates. It is said the city guards are wavering, just waiting for a chance to desert.
column2: 全城活力四射，喧嚣沸腾。关于进军$VarString1、夺取城门的传言满天飞。据说城防军已动摇，只待时机叛逃。

column1: The clash of weapons and shrieks of the dying echo off the buildings around you. Running hard down the side streets of $PlaceName, you wonder which way to leave the city.
column2: 武器相击与临终惨叫在你周围的楼宇间回响。你沿着$PlaceName的侧街拼命奔跑，思索着如何逃离此城。

column1: The clergy of the $cityChurch $Support3 change in the government.
column2: $cityChurch的教士$Support3政府中的变动。

column1: The cleric is impressed, and promises to reconsider his views. You have gained some influence.
column2: 教士颇为赞赏，允诺重新审视其立场。你已赢得些许影响力。

column1: The clerk asks a novice to escort you to a small tower where a few dedicated monks pursue alchemical experiments. At the entrance, some of the monks ask penetrating questions about alchemy. Tongue-tied, you find yourselves unable to answer.
column2: 书记官命一名学徒护送你前往一座小塔，那里有几位虔诚僧侣从事炼金实验。入口处，部分僧侣提出尖锐的炼金问题。你一时语塞，竟无法作答。

column1: The clerk asks a novice to escort you to a small tower where a few dedicated monks pursue alchemical experiments. At the entrance, some of the monks ask penetrating questions, but apparently your intellectual abilities, knowledge of alchemy, or simple speaking skills impress them sufficiently. Finally, after more discussion, you are introduced to the leader of alchemical researches.
column2: 书记官命一名学徒护送你前往一座小塔，那里有几位虔诚僧侣从事炼金实验。入口处，僧侣们接连发问，但显然，你的才智、炼金知识或口才足以令他们满意。经过一番讨论，你终于得见炼金研究的领袖。

column1: The clerk carefully examines your letter of credit in a strong light. He nods once, then briefly disappears. When he returns, he carries a weighty purse. He sits down in front of you and counts out the full amount of the note, $Money1.
column2: 书记官在强光下仔细查验你的信用票据。他点头示意，随即短暂离去。归来时，手中已持一袋沉重的钱币。他坐于你面前，逐一清点出票据全额，$Money1。

column1: The clerk considers your request, then shrugs.
column2: 书记官考虑了你的请求，随后耸肩。

column1: The clerk laughs. "We could discuss politics all day and reach no conclusions. I am a busy man. My superiors are even busier. Trouble someone less busy with your importunate lobby."
column2: 书记官笑道：“我们纵谈一日，也难有定论。我事务繁忙，上司更忙。若欲游说，不妨找个不那么忙的人。”

column1: The clerk nods, admitting the justice of your arguments.
column2: 书记官点头，承认你的论据确有道理。

column1: The clerk shrugs. "This is a monastery, not a guild. We have nothing for sale. All we provide is a safe haven for those accepted into the order, a place for relaxation and contemplation."
column2: 书记官耸肩：“这里是修道院，非公会。我们无物可售。惟为入会者提供安身之所，一处休憩与冥想之地。”

column1: The clerk sniffs and motions you toward the door. "I'm sorry, $NamedOneName is busy today. In fact, he's busy all week."
column2: 书记官鼻哼一声，示意你出门。“抱歉，$NamedOneName今日无暇。实则整周皆忙。”

column1: The clerk takes your money swiftly.
column2: 书记官迅速接过你的钱财。

column1: The clerk takes your money, somewhat disdainfully, shrugs, and puts it away.
column2: 书记官略带轻蔑地接过你的钱财，耸肩收起。

column1: The clerk's eyes turn to nasty slits.
column2: 书记官双目眯成两道凶狠的细缝。

column1: The clerks laugh in your face. Before you can protest, guards step forward with lowered halberds and poke you back out the door. You stumble backwards down the steps and fall into a mud puddle! Red-faced, you wipe yourselves off and move away down a side street.
column2: 书记官当面大笑。你尚未抗议，卫兵已挺戟上前，将你推出门外。你踉跄退下台阶，跌入泥坑！你红着脸擦净身子，沿侧街离去。

column1: The clerks laugh in your faces. Before you can protest, guards step forward with lowered halberds and poke you back out the door. You stumble backwards down the steps and fall into a mud puddle! Red-faced, you wipe yourselves off and stumble away down a side street.
column2: 书记官当面大笑。你尚未抗议，卫兵已挺戟上前，将你推出门外。你踉跄退下台阶，跌入泥坑！你红着脸擦净身子，沿侧街蹒跚而去。

column1: The cloaked figure throws back her hood and smiles. She's a chisel-faced young blonde who looks strong and dangerous.
column2: 那名披斗篷的女子掀开兜帽，嫣然一笑。她面容棱角分明，金发碧眼，显得刚毅而危险。

column1: The clothmakers $Support6 changes.
column2: 织布匠$Support6更替。

column1: The clothmakers' guild $VarPhrase7 change in the government.
column2: 织布匠公会$VarPhrase7于政局中更迭。

column1: The combined strength of the caravan discourages any robbers or bandits, while the merchants know enough of local politics to avoid feuds and wars.
column2: 商队的强大阵容足以震慑劫匪与盗贼，而商人们亦谙熟当地政局，避开了纷争与战祸。

column1: The contestants face each other, then charge forward at a mighty gallop, each one aiming a blunted lance at the other's shield.
column2: 参赛者彼此对峙，随即策马疾驰，各自以钝矛直指对方之盾。

column1: The contestants rein in their horses, dismount, and meet to discuss the match.
column2: 参赛者勒马下鞍，相会商议比武之事。

column1: The copper knob.
column2: 铜制圆钮。

column1: The corpse of a man in armor lies near. You recognize it as your acquaintance, $NamedOneName. Poor fellow! He met the dragon one last time, but as he suspected, he did not come off the victor.
column2: 一具披甲男尸近旁横卧。你认出那是你的故交，$NamedOneName。可怜之人！他终与恶龙再战一场，然如其所料，未能胜出。

column1: The craft tied to the piers and wharves have many destinations. Some are available now because they leave today. Others leave later in the week; they will not take passengers until the day of departure. Overall, your options are...
column2: 停泊于码头与栈桥之舟，去向各异。有者即刻启航，亦有稍后方行，临行始载客。综观诸般选择，则……

column1: The creature is a schrat, a wild man. He is nude except for his shaggy hair and a rawhide pouch.
column2: 此物乃施拉特，一名野人。唯披蓬乱长发，腰悬生皮囊，赤身裸体。

column1: The crone dribbles and shrieks, "No man can undo what Satan hath done! You are doomed! I call the curse of Hell over you. Damned souls, awake!"
column2: 老妪口吐涎沫，尖声嘶叫：“撒旦所为，岂有人能解？尔等必死无疑！我召地狱之诅咒加诸汝身。受谴之魂，醒吧！”

column1: The cross's destruction enabled the dragon to return, and it has done so. Now you must face the monstrous $NamedTwoName in person -- a much tougher test than an insane priest.
column2: 十字架既毁，恶龙遂返，今须亲迎此巨兽$NamedTwoName——其难远胜癫狂祭司。

column1: The crowd at the $councilHall jeers when the $CityLordTitle appears on an upstairs balcony. He replies by ordering his guards to fire on the crowd, which retreats to the other side of the $citySquare. They start a siege, so you...
column2: 当$councilHall之上出现$CityLordTitle时，围观者嗤笑不已。彼则命卫士向众开火，众人退至$citySquare另一侧。围城之势已起，于是……

column1: The crowd has surrounded the $fortress, and loudly demands entrance and the surrender of $CityLordTitle. The guards on the walls appear nervous, and perhaps willing to surrender. You...
column2: 围众已将$fortress团团围住，高呼入内并逼降$CityLordTitle。城上守军神色紧张，似有意投降。于是……

column1: The crowd murmurs, uncertain of this strange behavior, but lets the rebel leaders leave the building. The sergeant's guardsmen tie their hands, and you lead them all away.
column2: 观众窃窃私语，不解此举，然任叛首离楼。军曹麾下兵卒缚其手，尔率众而去。

column1: The crowd roars approval. One fat woman grins and says, "The Great Monastery. Isn't that $MonasteryLocation?" Your reply is drowned out by the chanting.
column2: 群众欢呼雀跃。一肥妇咧嘴笑道：“大修道院。莫非便是$MonasteryLocation？”尔之答语已被喧哗淹没。

column1: The crying of a young girl attracts your attention. You listen and hear...
column2: 少女啼哭引尔注目。细听之下，闻……

column1: The cultists recapture you and, without further ado, sacrifice you to their evil deity. You die, but perhaps your souls go up to Heaven.
column2: 教徒复擒尔，不容分说，便将尔献祭于邪神。尔虽殒命，然魂或升天。

column1: The cultists run away, leaving you alone beside their now-guttering fire, and their unholy altar.
column2: 教徒四散奔逃，只余你独对渐熄的篝火与那亵渎的祭坛。

column1: The curse on the land afflicts even the unliving.
column2: 土地之诅咒，连无生命之物亦难逃其害。

column1: The dark streets still have occasional carts moving and porters dashing about, all because of the fair. In the flickering lamplight you turn toward...
column2: 黑暗街巷间，仍偶见车辇穿梭，苦力奔走，皆因集市所致。微光摇曳中，尔转而望向……

column1: The darkness blinds your eyes, and the taste of ash binds your tongue as you attempt the words of the prayer. There is no response from the heavens.
column2: 黑暗蒙蔽双目，灰烬之味紧缚舌端，尔欲诵经，却无回应自天而降。

column1: The days pass peacefully and quickly. Soon you are at agreed-upon parting point, the gates of $NearestCity.
column2: 日子平静而飞逝。转瞬之间，你已抵达约定的离别之地——$NearestCity的城门。

column1: The deacon accepts your offering gracefully. "Heaven values all gifts, and clearly your hearts are in the right place," he intones.
column2: 执事优雅接纳尔之供奉。“天庭珍视一切馈赠，尔等诚心可见一斑。”彼低声道。

column1: The deacon is impressed with the sum you proffer. "Would that all men and women were as generous," he opines. "Then would the kingdom of heaven on earth be fulfilled much more speedily, and the millenium be at hand."
column2: 执事见尔所献数额，颇为赞叹。“若世人皆如此慷慨，天国在世之愿便可速达，千年盛世亦可近矣。”彼慨然言道。

column1: The deacon is pleased as he accepts your donation. "I will add this to the daily coffers," says he. "Soon we will have sufficient funds to truly serve our congregation."
column2: 执事欣然收下尔之捐赠。“此款将归入日常库藏，”彼曰，“不久我们便有足够的资财，足以真正庇护教众。”

column1: The deacon's eyes bulge when he sees the sum you offer. "This is indeed a generous donation," he cries. "May all the saints bless you!"
column2: 执事见尔所献巨款，双目圆睁。“此诚为慷慨之捐，”彼惊呼，“愿诸圣庇佑尔等！”

column1: The dead spiders ooze horrible fluids. Your weapons require careful cleaning; as soon as possible you resume your journey, in case more spiders show up.
column2: 死蛛渗出恶液。尔之兵刃需仔细清洗；尔当尽快启程，以防更多蜘蛛来袭。

column1: The defeat of the bandits makes this area safe once more, should you wish to stay and camp.
column2: 盗匪既平，此地重归安全，尔若愿留宿扎营，尽可如常。

column1: The demon guffaws, "The contract is binding. Legal authority is only applicable when a law has been broken."
column2: 恶魔狞笑：“契约既立，不可违背。法律之效，惟违法之时始显。”

column1: The demon laughs, "Defeat me!"
column2: 恶魔大笑：“败我吧！”

column1: The demon snorts, "So?"
column2: 恶魔冷哼：“何妨？”

column1: The demon speaks in a slow, hissing rumble. "Begone, humans," it growls, "or meet your doom at my hands." You...
column2: 恶魔低沉嘶吼：“滚吧，凡人，否则将遭我之灭顶之灾。”尔……

column1: The demon, sensing the threat, begins quoting huge tracts of German law, including canon law, to defend his position. While he is doing so, $NamedOneName turns to you.
column2: 恶魔察觉威胁，遂援引浩繁德意志律法，包括教会法，以自辩。其间，$NamedOneName转向尔。

column1: The demon, taken aback, states, "Nay! Thy usage of the bridge is tacit acceptance of the agreed terms."
column2: 恶魔愕然道：“休得胡言！汝等过桥，即默许协议条款。”

column1: The depredations of the raubritter (robber knight) to the $Direction are discussed by all. Everyone knows of someone who has been hurt by his activities.
column2: 关于盗骑士$Direction之劫掠，众皆议论纷纷。无人不知其暴行所伤之人。

column1: The depredations of the so-called robber knight $NamedOneName must be stopped! All brave men willing to face this bloodthirsty wolf are urged to present themselves to the $CityLordTitle without fail.
column2: 必须制止所谓盗骑士$NamedOneName之暴行！凡有胆敢直面此嗜血狼者，务请即刻投奔$CityLordTitle。

column1: The desperation of the situation makes it too difficult to concentrate on a prayer. You must act to decide the fate of these innocent victims.
column2: 局势危急，难专心祈祷。尔须出手，决断无辜受害者之命运。

column1: The devil-things shrug aside $ChosenOneName's attempt to summon saintly protection, and are among you with frightening speed. Now you must fight.
column2: 魔物轻蔑无视$ChosenOneName祈求圣佑之举，旋即以骇人速度扑至尔前。尔唯有奋战。

column1: The docks are well barricaded and fortified by city guards. Although a few piers are still open for boats, every one is empty today. After looking around, you...
column2: 码头戒备森严，由城卫把守。虽尚有数处泊位开放，然今日皆空。环顾四周后，尔……

column1: The door has two knobs, gold and silver. One opens the door, the other is probably a trap. You press...
column2: 门上有两枚门把手，一金一银。一枚可开门，另一枚恐为陷阱。尔按……

column1: The door may hide a trap! You think, then press...
column2: 大门可能藏有陷阱！你思索片刻，随即按下……

column1: The door slams in your face.
column2: 门砰然关上，挡于尔前。

column1: The doormen scowl.
column2: 守门人怒目而视。

column1: The doormen scowl. "Mangy dogs! We have no use for you here. Begone."
column2: 守门人怒目而视。“贱狗！此处无需尔等。滚开！”

column1: The dragon backs into its lair. You follow, cautiously.
column2: 恶龙退回巢穴。尔谨慎尾随。

column1: The dragon immediately rips $ChosenOneName into seven pieces and devours $him completely. It then states, "Now you are mine own children. Begone from this place." There is a puff of smoke, and suddenly the room vanishes around you; you appear miles away.
column2: 恶龙立即将$ChosenOneName撕裂七块，并将你吞食殆尽。继而曰：“尔等今为吾子。速离此地。”烟雾一缕，室中忽空，尔已置身数里之外。

column1: The dragon is angry at your impertinence, and its eyes flash. But it acquiesces, pulls back, coils up and becomes inert stone. It is gone, for now, and perhaps for centuries to come.
column2: 恶龙怒于尔之无礼，双目炯炯。然终屈服，退缩蜷伏，化为顽石。暂且离去，或许数百年不再现身。

column1: The dragon is angry at your impertinence, and its eyes flash. But it does not strike. Instead, it coils up on its gold and goes to sleep. The beast and horde fade, seemingly turning to stone.
column2: 恶龙怒于尔之无礼，双目炯炯。然未出手，仅盘踞金座，沉睡不动。妖兽与群皆消散，仿佛化作石像。

column1: The dragon is angry at your impertinence, and its eyes flash. But rather than strike, it coils up in its lair and becomes comatose -- like stone. It may sleep for centuries.
column2: 恶龙怒于尔之无礼，双目炯炯。然不击，反蜷伏巢中，陷入昏迷——宛如石像。或可长眠数百年。

column1: The dragon is angry at your impertinence. But its lust for the cup proves too great. It snatches the cup from your grip and returns it to its hoard. Then it coils up and seems to turn to stone as it goes back to endless sleep.
column2: 恶龙怒于尔之无礼。然贪杯之心更甚，夺杯而去，归入宝库。继而蜷缩，似化为石，重返无尽长眠。

column1: The dragon lashes out in an explosion of fire and frenzy that leaves you bleeding on the ground. You look up to see it flapping off, wreathed in flames.
column2: 恶龙骤然喷火发狂，尔身负重伤，倒地不起。抬首只见其裹挟烈焰，振翅而去。

column1: The dragon's jaws close on the horse's back, breaking it with a single snap. The monster flies off with its prize. The surviving horses are foam-covered and panting with fear.
column2: 恶龙巨颚合拢，一口咬断马背，怪物携获物腾空而去。幸存之马浑身白沫，惊惧喘息。

column1: The dread lord of the castle bleeds out his life at your feet, his brutal men dead or fled. As the sun rises, the grateful peasants hail you as their savior, and set fire to the castle as revenge upon those who persecuted them.
column2: 城堡之主鲜血淋漓，命丧尔足下，其悍卒或亡或遁。旭日初升，感恩之农夫称尔为救星，并纵火焚堡，以报昔日迫害之仇。

column1: The dread lord of the castle lies dead, his brutal men either killed or fled. As the sun rises, the grateful peasants hail you as their savior, and set fire to the castle as revenge upon those who persecuted them.
column2: 城堡之主已死，其悍卒或亡或遁。旭日东升，感恩之农夫称尔为救星，并纵火焚堡，以报昔日迫害之仇。

column1: The dreadful Wild Hunter himself comes forth at your defeat. He waves his spear over $ChosenOneName, who is suddenly torn to pieces by ravaging hellhounds. "Now I have the soul I wished for, and I shall depart. We may not meet again, brash mortals, but I suspect you'll remember me."
column2: 惊怖之荒野猎人亲自现身于尔之败北之际。彼挥枪一扫，$ChosenOneName瞬间被噬魂恶犬撕裂。“今吾得所求之魂，将告辞。尔等凡人，或无缘再见，然我料尔等必记吾名。”

column1: The dwarf agonizes, but greed wins out. He mumbles,
column2: 矮人苦闷不已，然贪欲终胜。他喃喃道，

column1: The dwarf agonizes, but terror wins out. He mumbles,
column2: 矮人苦闷不已，然恐惧终胜。他喃喃道，

column1: The dwarf claps a red cap on his head and vanishes, taking the potions with him.
column2: 矮人将一顶红帽扣于头上，携药剂遁去。

column1: The dwarf king pulls out a gorgeous steel cuirass and offers it to you. It is a bribe so you'll leave the mines! Do you ...
column2: 矮人王取出一件华丽的钢制胸甲，向你递来。这是贿赂，只为让你离开矿坑！你是否……

column1: The dwarf looks over the lip of the pit and cackles,
column2: 矮人俯瞰坑沿，咯咯笑道，

column1: The dwarf points at $ChosenOneName! Appalled, you decide to...
column2: 矮人指向$ChosenOneName！你惊骇不已，决定……

column1: The dwarf responds,
column2: 矮人答道，

column1: The dwarf stamps his foot, claps a red cap on his head and vanishes. Immediately, clouds of green mist pour from the roof, the walls, and the floor. Your eyes and throat burn -- it's poison! Quickly you...
column2: 矮人顿足，戴上一顶红帽，随即消失。顷刻间，绿色雾气自屋顶、墙壁与地面滚滚涌出。你双眼与喉部灼痛——这是毒气！你迅速……

column1: The dwarf thinks over your proposal, then agrees to talk, saying,
column2: 矮人思量你的提议，旋即应允交谈，言道：

column1: The dwarf's laugh is like metal cracking.
column2: 矮人的笑声如金属碎裂。

column1: The earth quakes and cracks. A dragon squirms its way up through the soil like a grotesque worm from Hell. It turns its fearsome snout toward you as the earth around it glows red hot.
column2: 大地震颤裂开。一条巨龙如地狱中的怪虫般从泥土中蜿蜒而出。它狰狞的鼻口转向你，周遭大地炽红如火。

column1: The effects of the potion leave the knights helpless, and you quickly and calmly make your way through the open door to freedom.
column2: 药剂之效使骑士们无力抵抗，你从容穿过敞开的门，逃出生天。

column1: The eloquent plea of $ChosenOneName is so manifestly virtuous that even the bishop's heart is moved.
column2: $ChosenOneName的恳切陈情显见其德，连主教亦为之动容。

column1: The enemy has a sacred relic? No wonder the dwarfs (always vulnerable to Christian symbols) cannot defeat them! But you, sturdy humans, are not repelled by such! Onward!
column2: 敌人竟持有圣物？难怪矮人们（素来畏怯基督教符号）无法取胜！然汝等坚毅之人，岂会被此所阻？前行吧！

column1: The entire inn is rocked by a gigantic explosion. People, bedding, and splintered furniture flies in all directions.
column2: 整座客栈被巨响震撼，人、床褥与碎木四散飞溅。

column1: The entire wall of this corridor is lined with rows of animal horns, like some strange trophy room of a mad hunter. There are goat horns, ram horns, stag horns, bull horns, and a set of horns from an animal you cannot identify. You...
column2: 此走廊整面墙皆列满兽角，宛如疯猎人之奇珍陈列室。有山羊角、公羊角、鹿角、牛角，还有一对你不识其种的角。你……

column1: The entrance to the stately and well-appointed anterooms of the $councilHall for $PlaceName is well guarded. You...
column2: 这座为$PlaceName而设的$councilHall庄严雅致的前厅入口戒备森严。你……

column1: The evil $NamedOneName, the robber knight who terrorized the country, lies bleeding out his life before you. Demoralized, his men drop their weapons and surrender. You begin the pleasant task of picking through the castle's treasury. You speculate about how often future travellers will bless your name for the road's safety.
column2: 那作恶多端的劫匪骑士$NamedOneName，正于你面前血流不止，奄奄一息。其麾下士卒军心尽丧，弃械投降。你遂着手清理城堡库藏，心中暗忖未来旅人将因道路平安而几度称颂汝名。

column1: The exhausted caravan guards hail you warmly. "For a minute there," says their leader, "we thought you were a holy army, descending upon those vermin like a cleansing fire. After they fled, we realized it was a trick of the sunlight."
column2: 疲惫不堪的商队护卫热情迎你。“方才片刻，”领队说道，“我们还以为你是天降神兵，如烈火般扫荡那群害虫。待他们逃窜，方知不过是阳光作祟。”

column1: The exploding potion completely confuses the pirates, giving everyone a chance to escape into the woods. The pirates, after bumbling about for a bit, content themselves with looting the riverboat of its cargo.
column2: 爆炸药剂令海盗大乱，众人趁机遁入林中。海盗摸索一阵后，只得转而掠夺河船货物。

column1: The exploding potion stops the guards for a few minutes. You try vainly to get over the wall before they recover, but you lack the necessary skill. When the potion's effects end, the guards close in and attack.
column2: 爆炸药剂使守卫一时失措。你试图趁其未及恢复翻越城墙，却苦无技艺。药效一过，守卫便合围攻来。

column1: The explosion of fire panics the schrats, who immediately flee in all directions -- one of them is burning like a torch, and all are screaming their terror.
column2: 火焰爆炸惊得妖精四散奔逃——其中一只如火炬般燃烧，众皆凄厉尖叫。

column1: The farmers bow and nod politely, impressed but frightened by your appearance and self-confidence. Despite $his best efforts, $ChosenOneName is unable to get any useful information except the name of this place: $PlaceName.
column2: 农民恭敬颔首，既钦佩又畏惧于你的威仪与自信。尽管你的竭力探问，$ChosenOneName仍未能获知任何有用信息，唯知此地名为$PlaceName。

column1: The fervent prayers of $ChosenOneName rise above the witches' howl, but there is no response from $NamedOneName.
column2: $ChosenOneName的虔诚祷告盖过女巫的嚎叫，然$NamedOneName并无回应。

column1: The fight is hard, but you are triumphant. However, all the commotion has drawn other interested parties in your direction, and you'd prefer not to take on the whole Sabbat! You move away fast.
column2: 战斗艰难，然终获胜。然而喧嚣引得旁人趋至，你不愿与整个女巫集会正面交锋！速速撤离。

column1: The fight is over and you have won. Sir $NamedOneName, the glory-seeking knight, kneels before you, bleeding and gasping for breath. $ChosenOneName tells him, "It is wrong for human to fight human when the dragon still rages and innocent folk are its prey. Our foe is the monster, not one another."
column2: 战事已毕，你凯旋。好战的骑士$NamedOneName跪伏于你膝前，鲜血淋漓，气息微弱。$ChosenOneName劝诫道：“当巨龙肆虐、无辜百姓沦为猎物之时，人类相残实属不义。吾等之敌乃怪物，而非彼此。”

column1: The fight with his men allowed the nobleman to escape. You realize that this incident may not help your local reputation.
column2: 与随从激战之际，贵族得以脱身。你意识到此事恐损汝当地声望。

column1: The fighting is over, and you are still standing. Unfortunately, the city wall now crawls with guards bearing torches. You cannot get to the wall unseen. One man cries out from atop the wall, "We must be more alert. Those fellows nearly got through!"
column2: 战斗结束，你犹屹立不倒。不幸的是，城墙上此刻遍布持炬守卫。你无法悄然攀上城墙。一人于城头高呼：“须更加警觉！那些家伙险些闯入！”

column1: The first time, a bee stings him; the second time, he slips into the stream; the third time, he is seized by a sneezing fit halfway through, and so on. Though it seems to the assemblage that you have undergone the ceremony, in fact you come away feeling none of the taint you expected. The saint has protected you!
column2: 初次被蜂蜇，第二次滑入溪流，第三次半途打喷嚏，如此反复。众人虽以为汝已受礼，实则毫无预期之污秽感。圣徒庇佑于汝！

column1: The flames begin to crackle about your feet as $ChosenOneName finishes $his prayer. The fire rises higher and higher, but you feel no heat. You all stand there, in the blaze, smiling at the Templars.
column2: 当$ChosenOneName诵毕你的祷文时，火焰已在汝足畔噼啪作响。火势愈升愈烈，然汝全然不觉灼热。众人伫立火中，向圣殿骑士微笑致意。

column1: The flight is short, and soon $ChosenOneName returns. No one pays any further attention to you, and you leave quickly.
column2: 逃亡短暂，$ChosenOneName旋即归来。无人再留意于汝，汝遂匆匆离去。

column1: The floor, covered with gore, looks very slick. You may wish to remove some of your armor and other encumbrance before making the attempt to run across while dodging the ice and flames.
column2: 地面血迹斑斑，极为湿滑。汝或可卸下部分甲胄与负重，再冒险穿越冰焰之间。

column1: The foes lie dead before you, their blood decorating the altar upon which they so recently performed their foul rites. Quickly you bless this spot and leave.
column2: 敌人尸横于前，其血染红了他们不久前尚行邪术的祭坛。汝速速祝圣此地，继而离去。

column1: The footing here is extremely difficult. Everyone in the party suffers as you slip and slide your way over rough rocks and sharp stones, down to the ground.
column2: 此处地势艰险异常。众人于嶙峋岩石与尖锐砾石间踉跄滑行，直至谷底。

column1: The foreign traders $Support5 change.
column2: 外国商人$Support5更替。

column1: The foreign traders are less important than a guild, as are various banking and trading concerns, such as the Hanseatic League, the Fugger Bank, and the Medici Bank.
column2: 外国商人地位不及商会，亦逊于各类银行与贸易机构，如汉萨同盟、富格尔银行与美第奇银行。

column1: The four mutter among themselves momentarily, in response to your request. The one in the red robes seems to be the leader, and he is shaking his head vigorously. Suddenly, before you can do more than shout in alarm, the four bolt back down the path, bawling in fear. You are left standing alone on the path.
column2: 四人闻言低声商议。着红袍者似为首，频频摇头。猝不及防，汝方惊呼未毕，四人已沿路狂奔，惶恐哀号。汝独留于道。

column1: The four strangers converse among themselves. "Very well," says the man in red. "Make sure you go soon to the initiations." He nods to the wolf, and the beast lets you all pass. The others point vaguely in the direction of the stream, then hurry off to their own business, leaving you in the middle of the field.
column2: 四名异客窃窃私语。“罢了，”红衣者道，“务必尽快赴任。”他点头示意狼群，狼遂放行汝等。余者遥指溪流方向，匆匆离去，汝独处旷野。

column1: The four strangers goggle at your excuses. "I knew it!" cries the nobleman. "They are unbelievers! Slay them!" And with that, the wolf -- aided by the others -- attacks.
column2: 四名异客瞪视汝之辩解。“我就知道！”贵族怒喝，“他们是异教徒！杀之！”于是，狼群携其余同伙一齐扑来。

column1: The friar and his followers are gone. Although everybody hates the "pardoners," it is still a serious sin to attack a cleric. You can almost physically feel the loss of favor and virtue.
column2: 修士及其追随者已去。虽众皆憎“赦罪者”，然袭击教士仍属大罪。汝几乎能真切感受到失宠与德行之损。

column1: The friar collapses, sobbing. You leave him there, with his followers gathered all around, quite confused.
column2: 修士瘫倒在地，啜泣不止。汝将其遗于原地，随从环绕，茫然无措。

column1: The friar gloats over your fallen forms.
column2: 修士幸灾乐祸于汝等颓然之状。

column1: The friar gloats. "Ah, see the power and justice of Our Lord. Unbelievers who attack me reveal themselves."
column2: 修士洋洋得意：“看啊，我主之权柄与正义！攻击我的异教徒终露原形。”

column1: The friar is delighted to have an escort.
column2: 修士欣然得护送。

column1: The friar seems aghast at his words, but is unable to say anything but the truth. His followers are so angry they begin beating him. You shrug and go on, knowing his fate is richly deserved.
column2: 修士闻言愕然，却只能坦言真相。其徒愤怒至极，竟殴打其师。汝耸肩而去，深知其咎由自取。

column1: The friar smiles. "Ah, a wise choice, noble ones." He gets out a portable altar, sprinkles you with holy water from a rusty, decrepit asper, intones a variety of prayers, and then has you kiss the Letter of Indulgence which he carries.
column2: 修士微笑：“明智之举，诸位贵人。”他取出便携祭坛，以锈蚀破旧的洒圣水器为你洒圣水，诵念诸般祷文，复令汝亲吻随身携带的赎罪证书。

column1: The friar wishes you a good journey also. You move off, and soon they disappear behind you.
column2: 修士亦祝汝旅途顺遂。汝启程远行，不久彼等便隐于身后。

column1: The gate is closed for the night, with guards patrolling above and below.
column2: 夜幕降临，城门紧闭，上下皆有守卫巡逻。

column1: The gate is heavily guarded, but most of the guards are watching for people trying to get into the city illegally, not for those trying to leave.
column2: 城门戒备森严，然守卫多防非法入城者，非拒离城者。

column1: The gate opens before you, and waves of bitter gas rush out over you. A foul, dry stink fills the air. You step forward and see weird gases floating over a dimly-glowing flooring. You must pick your steps carefully.
column2: 城门为你开启，阵阵恶臭气体扑面而来。空气中弥漫着刺鼻干涩之味。汝向前一步，只见幽光闪烁的地面上漂浮着诡异烟雾。汝须步步为营。

column1: The gate sergeant growls, "Keep a close watch, boys. Whoever did that may try again."
column2: 门卫咆哮：“小子们，盯紧点！那干坏事的可能还会再来。”

column1: The gate slowly opens before you, without even being touched. A hollow voice echoes, "Thou hast all the Six Keys. Canst thou halt the Apocalypse?" You cautiously enter the chamber.
column2: 城门缓缓开启，未曾触及。空洞之声回荡：“汝已集齐六钥，可止末日乎？”汝谨慎步入密室。

column1: The ghost does not appear to understand, and you feel the fear of its presence grow upon you like the rising tide.
column2: 幽灵似乎不解，汝只觉其阴森之气如潮水般渐涨，令人胆寒。

column1: The ghost nods eagerly, and points. You'd not have seen it yourselves, but once it's pointed out, you spy a fallen gravestone hidden beneath a tangle of brambles. Working swiftly, you cut away the vines and right the stone. The ghost cries out joyously and vanishes!
column2: 幽灵急切地点了点头，并指向一处。若非它指点，你们本难察觉，如今拨开荆棘丛，便见一块倾倒的墓碑。你迅速割去藤蔓，扶正石碑。幽灵欢声雀跃，随即消逝！

column1: The ghost nods.
column2: 幽灵点了点头。

column1: The girl you have rescued falls at your feet. "Thank you, thank you," she sobs. "I can never repay your bravery and kindness." You help her up and advise her to leave the area. She tells you she can live with her aunt, a few days away, and departs. You proceed on your way.
column2: 你救下的少女扑倒在你脚下。“多谢，多谢！”她泣不成声，“你的英勇与仁慈，我无以为报。”你扶起她，劝她离开此地。她言自己可投奔几日路程外的姑母，遂辞别而去。你继续前行。

column1: The gold knob.
column2: 黄金旋钮。

column1: The graveyard is calm and silent. A small boquet of flowers rests on one of the stones. You get a sense of peace standing here, and you realize that to fear death is foolish: the kingdom of heaven awaits the virtuous. You ...
column2: 墓园静谧无声。一石之上，置有小小花束。伫立其间，心生安宁，方悟惧死实属愚昧：天国之门，为善者所开。你……

column1: The graveyard is not so well-kept as it first appeared: as you enter, you notice a dark grayness that covers everything. The sun goes behind a cloud, and a cold wind springs up from nowhere.
column2: 墓园远非初见那般整洁：步入其中，但觉周遭尽覆灰暗。太阳隐入云后，冷风骤起，无处不在。

column1: The groggy guild master peers through a window shutter.
column2: 醒盹的公会会长透过窗扉窥视。

column1: The groggy street leader peers through a window shutter.
column2: 醒盹的街坊首领透过窗扉窥视。

column1: The grotesque schrat grins broadly, then reaches into his rawhide pouch, pulling out a bizarre round fruit that you have never seen before. It glows with a greenish light. The schrat grunts encouragingly. It seems to be trying to reward you. Which of you will eat the strange fruit?
column2: 怪异的施拉特咧嘴大笑，随即探手入其牛皮囊，取出一枚从未见过的奇异圆果。果上泛着青光。施拉特低吼以示鼓励，似欲馈赠于你。诸君，谁愿食此奇果？

column1: The ground is just too slippery, and all of you are sliding and falling down as you struggle across the slimy blood. The fire gives you some fairly serious injuries, while the freezing sleet penetrates to the marrow of your bones. All too slowly, you gain the other side of the cavern.
column2: 地面过于湿滑，众人挣扎穿行于黏稠血泊时，纷纷滑倒。火焰灼伤甚重，而冰霰直透骨髓。缓慢至极，终抵洞窟彼岸。

column1: The guard captain growls in dismay and quickly puts his sword to the throat of $ChosenOneName. "Cease or die," he says.
column2: 卫队长愤然低吼，迅即以剑刃抵住$ChosenOneName喉间。“止步，否则死！”他喝道。

column1: The guard corporal leans out the door and hisses, "Dogs like you aren't fit to set foot inside this bank. Begone!"
column2: 卫兵下士探身门外，嘶声道：“尔等贱民，岂配踏入此银库？速退！”

column1: The guard leader smiles. "Men," he says, addressing his troop, "we need to investigate that corner most carefully!" He leads them away to a far corner of the building, ignoring you completely.
column2: 卫队首领微笑道：“诸君，”他对部众言，“须仔细查勘那隅！”遂率众移往楼角，全然不理睬你。

column1: The guard leader turns purple. "What, take money from scum like you?" he roars. "You think our loyalty to $PlaceName can be bought with a few coins?"
column2: 卫队首领面色铁青。“竟向尔等败类收钱？”他怒吼，“莫非以为吾等对$PlaceName之忠，可凭区区铜板买得？”

column1: The guard scowls and cries, "Ho, enemies at the gate!" As the fortress comes awake, you quickly retreat to the dark forest to avoid recognition. Quietly, you discuss the best course once dawn comes.
column2: 卫兵怒斥：“敌袭城门！”堡垒惊醒之际，你疾速遁入密林，以免被识破。天明之后，悄然商议对策。

column1: The guard sergeant inspects your coins and his lip curls. "Trying to bribe an official of mighty $PlaceName, eh? Boys, capture those felons!"
column2: 卫兵中士验过汝等钱币，唇角微掀。“妄图贿赂雄踞$PlaceName之官吏乎？弟兄们，拿下此等歹徒！”

column1: The guard shakes his head. "Good job," you say smoothly, and your party continues on its way.
column2: 卫兵摇头。“干得好，”你从容说道，一行人继续前行。

column1: The guards are startled, but one of them reacts with blinding speed -- and actually catches the bottle! Eyeing it suspiciously, he cries, "This is alchemical magic -- they meant to slay us!"
column2: 卫兵猝不及防，然一人反应迅捷——竟接住了酒瓶！他疑神疑鬼，喊道：“这是炼金之术——他们意欲加害于我！”

column1: The guards are surprised but unsuspecting: when the vial breaks on the table, the bang and flash startle them, and the smoke chokes and blinds them. Utterly helpless, they fall to their knees.
column2: 卫兵虽惊却未防备：药瓶一碎，爆响与闪光令其惊惶，浓烟熏呛，致其失明。无助跪地。

column1: The guards arrest you all. Dejectedly, you troop off to the dungeon. One guard gloats, "The magistrate will properly see to you scum."
column2: 卫兵将汝等悉数逮捕。沮丧之间，押赴地牢。一卫兵幸灾乐祸：“法官自会处置尔等贱民。”

column1: The guards at the gate of $PlaceName are numerous and nervous. Some collect tolls from each person; your party would pay $Money1. Other guards watch the crowd while fingering the hilts of their weapons.
column2: $PlaceName城门守卫众多且紧张。有人向每位行人征收费用，汝等需付$Money1。另有卫兵手持兵器，注视人群。

column1: The guards begin to strip your unconscious bodies. Before they are through, however, the sergeant comes by and yells at them.
column2: 卫兵开始剥去汝等昏迷之躯的衣物。未及完成，中士忽至，厉声呵斥。

column1: The guards bow and step aside. "Enter, masters," they say. "Satan protect you."
column2: 卫兵鞠躬让路。“请进，诸位大人，”他们道，“撒旦庇佑尔等。”

column1: The guards brush off your approach. "Who are you?" sneers the sergeant. "Pay up or begone!" Behind you an impatient peasant grumbles about ignorant foreigners holding up the line.
column2: 卫兵轻蔑地挡驾：“汝等何人？”中士讥讽道，“交费则留，否则滚！”身后农夫不耐，抱怨无知外乡人阻塞通道。

column1: The guards have downed you.
column2: 卫兵已将汝等击倒。

column1: The guards lie in widening pools of blood and the cleaning woman flees; you press forward into the dark building...
column2: 卫兵躺于血泊之中，清洁妇仓皇逃窜；汝等趁机潜入黑暗楼宇……

column1: The guards politely but firmly escort you back into the $citySquare.
column2: 卫兵礼貌而坚定地护送汝等重返$citySquare。

column1: The guards politely but firmly escort you back out the front door and into the streets.
column2: 卫兵礼貌而坚定地护送汝等出大门，回归街市。

column1: The guards scowl and painstakingly question you for what seems like forever. In the end, unable to find a reason to exclude you, they grudgingly let you inside.
column2: 卫兵阴沉地质问汝等，反复盘查，久而未果，终勉强放行。

column1: The guards scowl at you and painstakingly question you for what seems like forever. In the end, unable to find any reason to exclude you, they grudgingly let you inside.
column2: 卫兵阴沉地质问汝等，反复盘查，久而未果，终勉强放行。

column1: The guards sergeant warns you that the $CityLordTitle is protected by a loyal personal guard, who must be overcome.
column2: 卫兵中士告诫汝等，$CityLordTitle由忠诚侍卫守护，须将其击败。

column1: The guards take you prisoner and march you off to prison. There, you will languish until your fate is decided.
column2: 卫兵将汝等囚禁，押赴狱中。汝等将在狱中煎熬，直至命运裁决。

column1: The guards, cowed, retreat in confusion. Their sergeant blurts out apologies. They stumble back around a corner and, when they think you can no longer see them, break into a run. You laugh and move along.
column2: 卫兵慑服，仓皇退却。中士连连道歉。他们绕过街角，待确信汝等不再看见，便拔腿狂奔。汝等一笑，继续前行。

column1: The guardsman inside recognizes you, as do several of his companions. "What can I do for you?" he asks. You...
column2: 内部卫兵认出汝等，同伴亦然。“有何差遣？”他问道。汝等……

column1: The guardsman snarls, "Troublesome scum! Take them away!"
column2: 卫兵咆哮：“麻烦的贱民！带走！”

column1: The guardsmen assume you are dead, and order some nearby civilians to dump your bodies in a midden outside the walls. There you awaken, a few hours later. All of your arms and armor have been taken, and most of your possessions. You crawl away from the foul heap and take stock of the situation.
column2: 卫兵误以为汝等已死，命附近平民将汝等尸首弃于城外粪坑。数小时后，汝等于此苏醒。武器甲胄尽失，财物亦多被夺。汝等爬离恶臭堆垛，审视处境。

column1: The guardsmen assume you are dead. They order some surrendered civilians to dump your bodies in a midden outside the walls. There you awaken, a few hours later. All of your arms, armor and obvious valuables are gone. You crawl off the stinking heap and take stock of your situation.
column2: 卫兵误以为汝等已死。命投降平民将汝等尸首弃于城外粪坑。数小时后，汝等于此苏醒。武器、甲胄及显见财物皆失。汝等爬离污秽堆垛，审视自身境况。

column1: The guardsmen quickly relieve you of weapons and armor, then herd you to the dungeons.
column2: 卫兵迅速缴械卸甲，继而驱赶汝等入地牢。

column1: The guardsmen suddenly lose heart. The crowd cheers as they flee. You are hoisted onto willing shoulders, everyone begins chanting slogans, and you all move toward $VarString1.
column2: 卫兵忽生怯意。人群欢呼，他们四散奔逃。汝等被抬上肩头，众人高呼口号，一行人向$VarString1进发。

column1: The guild courtyards are dark and quiet, while the guildsmen and their families sleep comfortably in upstairs bedrooms. You...
column2: 公会庭院幽暗寂静，公会成员及其家属安卧楼上寝室。汝等……

column1: The guild leader admits, "Yes, some of our members might be willing to teach certain skills. Let me inquire about which ones and the cost per day..."
column2: 公会会长坦言：“不错，部分会员或愿传授技艺。容我查问具体项目及日费……”

column1: The guild leader fastens you with a stare of ice. "What evidence do you have of such heinous crimes?"
column2: 公会会长以寒冰目光逼视汝等。“有何证据证明如此罪行？”

column1: The guild leader squares his shoulders and laughs in your face.
column2: 公会会长挺胸，当面哂笑。

column1: The guild leaders are not impressed. Their attitude remains that they $Support any changes in the government of $PlaceName.
column2: 公会会长对此不以为然。态度依旧，即$Support任何关于$PlaceName政府的变革。

column1: The guild masters currently $Support changes in the city government, but seem attentive as you speak. You...
column2: 公会会长目前$Support城市政府的变革，然汝等发言时，似颇为留意。汝等……

column1: The guildsmen are horrified by your allegations. However, when you give them the evidence, they promise to hold a special meeting to investigate the situation. It is clear that the meeting will produce a new guild leader.
column2: 公会成员闻汝等指控，无不震惊。然汝等出示证据后，他们允诺召开特别会议，彻查此事。显然，会议将选出新任公会会长。

column1: The gunsmith, in the daytime.
column2: 锻造师，白日里。

column1: The hairy forms of schrats charge from the trees, howling as they come. You have no choice but to draw weapons and defend yourselves.
column2: 施拉特毛茸茸的身影自林间冲出，嚎叫而来。汝等唯有拔剑自卫。

column1: The hamlet of $PlaceName nestles up against a hill. A small church sits amidst a graveyard. Smoke curls from the blacksmith's forge. Peasants labor in their fields and somewhere a dog barks.
column2: $PlaceName的小村依偎在山麓。一座小教堂矗立于墓地之中。铁匠铺里青烟袅袅。农夫在田间劳作，某处犬吠声起。

column1: The hapless gate guards clutch frantically at their eyes, temporarily devoid of sight. Moving quickly, you are already inside the gate before the befuddled guards think to crank it closed. One yells, "Magic! We've been attacked! Warn the officers." You keep running, and are out of sight before the Sunburst's effect wears off.
column2: 可怜的守门卫士慌乱地捂住双眼，一时失明。你动作迅捷，已在城门关闭之前闯入其中。一人高喊：“魔法！我们遭袭了！快去通报官吏！”你继续奔逃，待旭日术效力消散时已不见踪影。

column1: The heavens are silent. No reply comes to your pleas.
column2: 天空寂静无声。你的祈求未得回应。

column1: The heavens are silent. The choice is up to you.
column2: 天空依旧沉默。抉择权在你手中。

column1: The heavens fail to respond to your pleas. The darkness is unchanged.
column2: 天空对你的恳求毫无回应。黑暗未曾稍减。

column1: The heavens remain closed. No response is forthcoming.
column2: 天空依然紧闭。无人应答。

column1: The heavens remain silent. The saint does not see fit to answer you in your hour of need.
column2: 天空寂然无声。圣徒不愿在你危难之际垂听。

column1: The herbalist smiles and opens a triple-locked cabinet.
column2: 草药师微笑，开启一扇三重锁柜。

column1: The hermit indeed knows much about the saints, including one who was almost unknown to you. His stories are very enlightening.
column2: 隐士确知诸多圣徒之事，其中一位对你而言几近陌生。其言甚为启迪。

column1: The hermit's insights into the mysteries of your faith are quite rewarding. Some of you feel you have really learned something.
column2: 隐士对你信仰奥秘的洞见颇多裨益。诸君皆觉受益匪浅。

column1: The hermit's prayers are uplifting in their purity and holiness. In the beautiful, calm setting you experience a rare and unique sense of divine peace.
column2: 隐士的祈祷纯净而神圣，令人心生敬仰。身处幽静之境，你体验到难得的天赐安宁。

column1: The hideous minions howl behind you, but their hellish cries grow faint as you outdistance any pursuit.
column2: 可怖的爪牙在身后嚎叫，但随着你渐行渐远，那地狱般的嘶吼终归微弱。

column1: The holy saint responds to your plea by cracking open the side of the trap, making it easy for you to scramble up and out. Once out, you stop for a brief prayer of gratitude. As you do, you hear a sound as of stones crashing together. When you look, you see that the crack has closed up, leaving the trap as before.
column2: 圣徒回应你的祈愿，裂开陷阱一侧，使你得以攀出。脱困后，你驻足默祷致谢。忽闻石块相撞之声，回首只见裂缝复合，陷阱如初。

column1: The holzfrau smiles shyly and hugs each of you in turn, then flits off into the forest. You suspect you may see her again.
column2: 林女羞怯一笑，逐一拥抱众人，随即翩然遁入林间。你料她他日或再相见。

column1: The home of $NamedOneName, the government organizer, was attacked last night. However, his loyal supporters drove off the thugs. Most feel the attack was politically motivated.
column2: 政府组织者$NamedOneName的宅邸昨夜遇袭。然其忠仆击退暴徒。众皆疑此乃政治迫害。

column1: The home of $NamedTwoName, a well-known political agitator, was attacked last night. The thugs were driven off, but many feel they were government agents.
column2: 著名政治煽动者$NamedTwoName的宅邸昨夜遭袭。暴徒虽被驱离，然多以为系政府所为。

column1: The horror cackles madly with delight. "Your attempt to destroy my holy altar forces me to levy a harsh penitence. Prostrate yourselves before my glory!"
column2: 恐怖者狂笑不已：“汝等欲毁我圣坛，只得施以严惩。匍匐于吾荣耀之前！”

column1: The house is dark and somewhat forbidding-looking. You decide to ...
column2: 屋内阴暗，略显森然。你决定……

column1: The huge creature strides away into the storm, mounts its chariot, and rumbles away with the retreating storm clouds.
column2: 巨兽踏风而去，登其战车，随退去的雷云隆隆远逝。

column1: The human steps forward and says, "We can accept only one condition - you must help us defeat the dwarfs and the dreadful $NamedOneName, their slave lord. In any case, you must leave here at once!"
column2: 人类上前道：“我们只接受一项条件——汝须助我等击败矮人及其奴主$NamedOneName。无论如何，汝须即刻离去！”

column1: The human steps forward and says, "We can accept only one condition -- you must help us defeat the dwarfs and the dreadful $NamedOneName, their overlord. In any case, you must leave here at once!"
column2: 人类上前道：“我们只接受一项条件——汝须助我等击败矮人及其暴君$NamedOneName。无论如何，汝须即刻离去！”

column1: The huntsman accepts your money with a nod. "One week," he says, "then be gone."
column2: 猎户点头收下银两：“一周之后，便速速离开。”

column1: The huntsman and his soldiers escort (drag) you to the boundaries of the lord's domain. In the process, you are relieved of your money and weapons.
column2: 猎户及其兵卒护送（押解）你至领主疆界。途中，你被夺去钱财与武器。

column1: The huntsman and soldiers are defeated, but you know it's just a matter of time before more appear. While you can continue camping here for now, how long will you remain undisturbed?
column2: 猎户与兵卒虽败，然知援军将至。暂且可在此扎营，然能安身几何？

column1: The huntsman says, "In the countryside near here, certain persons are worried about a dragon."
column2: 猎户道：“此地乡野，有人忧惧巨龙。”

column1: The huntsman suddenly recognizes you.
column2: 猎户骤然认出你。

column1: The intensity of evil and danger here are too much for you. You decide to leave; someday you will have to find another such ceremony if you wish to bring about the ultimate defeat of the witches, but now is not the time.
column2: 此地邪气与险恶过甚，你决意离去；若欲彻底挫败女巫，他日自当另寻法会，今非其时。

column1: The intensity of evil and the danger here are too much for you. You decide to leave; someday you will have to find another such ceremony if you wish to bring about the ultimate defeat of the witches, but now is not the time.
column2: 此地邪气与危险过甚，你决意离去；若欲彻底挫败女巫，他日自当另寻法会，今非其时。

column1: The interior of the old ship is empty. Nothing remains here but the scorched pages of a huge book and a glass globe on the floor. You pick up the globe, inside of which swims a live trout, and leave.
column2: 古船内部空空如也。唯余一本巨册焦页及地上一只玻璃球。你拾起球中游曳的活鳟鱼，遂离去。

column1: The interior of the old ship is empty. Nothing remains here but the scorched pages of a huge book. You poke around for a few minutes, then leave.
column2: 古船内部空空如也。仅剩一本巨册焦页。你略作搜寻，旋即离去。

column1: The jewelers' guild $VarPhrase6 change in the city government.
column2: 宝石商行$VarPhrase6支持城市政权变革。

column1: The jewellers $Support5 change.
column2: 珠宝商$Support5支持变革。

column1: The juniormost clerk is at your elbow.
column2: 最年轻的书吏立于身旁。

column1: The kidnappers leave you for dead and take $ChosenOneName.
column2: 绑匪弃你于死地，携走$ChosenOneName。

column1: The knight begins to don his tournament armor, which you realize gives him the advantage of extra protection and a firmer seat on his horse.
column2: 骑士开始披挂比武甲胄，你方知此举既增防护，又稳坐马背。

column1: The knight gives your money to the nobleman, who grabs it quickly. "Hmph, about time!" he grumbles, then leads his party onward. You shrug off the encounter as bad luck and continue onward.
column2: 骑士将银两交予贵族，后者疾速攫取。“哼，总算到了！”他嘟囔一声，率队前行。你视此为厄运，继续赶路。

column1: The knight glowers, "Know that I, $NamedOneName, shall slay the fell beast $NamedTwoName myself. Begone! All the glory must be mine!"
column2: 骑士怒目而视：“尔等可知，吾$NamedOneName将亲斩恶兽$NamedTwoName。滚开！一切荣耀皆属吾！”

column1: The knight looks a little confused, "The road toll?" Then he collects himself, gives you a strong stare, and says, "Pay the toll, knaves!"
column2: 骑士略显困惑：“路税？”旋即镇定，凝视于你，喝道：“纳税吧，贱民！”

column1: The knight remarks upon your garments, saying that such heroes should not dress more poorly them himself, the defeated. He insists that you take a modest purse, to use in the nearest city. You gladly accept, and discover that he gave you five florins!
column2: 骑士评点你的衣着，谓英雄不应逊于己之败者。他坚持赠你一囊钱，以备赴近城之需。你欣然接受，方知内有五枚佛罗林！

column1: The knight rides off, and you resolve once more to gain sufficient fame that your names will remembered by generations yet unborn!
column2: 骑士策马远去，你决心再创功名，使后世永记汝等之名！

column1: The knight strikes $ChosenOneName truly, while your companion's blunted tip slides harmlessly off the edge of the knight's shield.
column2: 骑士正中$ChosenOneName，而同伴钝刃却滑落骑士盾沿，无伤于敌。

column1: The knight wheels his charger about, doffs his helmet in a gracious bow, and rides off happily. $ChosenOneName slowly staggers up from the dust and shakes $his head, dazed. You all chalk up the affair to experience and continue your travels.
column2: 骑士勒马回身，摘盔致礼，欢然离去。$ChosenOneName缓缓自尘土中站起，摇晃你的，神情恍惚。汝等视此为历练，继续前行。

column1: The knight's party passes like the train of the Emperor. He doesn't even glance in your direction!
column2: 骑士一行如皇驾般驶过，连看也不看你一眼！

column1: The knight's squire brings him your names, and he decides now is a good time for a brief camp. While you share a common resting place and fire, you eagerly ask him and his party about any news.
column2: 骑士侍从呈上汝等之名，骑士遂决定稍作歇息。同宿篝火旁，汝等急切询问其消息。

column1: The knight's squire rides up to discuss details. Quickly you discover that your names lack sufficient importance to concern this knight.
column2: 骑士侍从前来商议细节。你很快发现，汝等之名尚不足让此骑士在意。

column1: The knight's squire rides up to discuss your challenge. Your names are not unknown, and soon you agree on a course to be run around the nearby fields, woods and streams.
column2: 骑士侍从前来商讨挑战事宜。汝等之名并非全然陌生，不久便议定绕附近田畴林溪竞速之途。

column1: The knight, compelled by saintly power, answers truthfully: "Yes," he says, "there is a secret door in the east wall." He describes its operation; neither he nor his companions appear to think anything of what he has said.
column2: 骑士受圣力驱使，如实答曰：“是的，东墙有一密门。”他详述其机关；他与随从对此毫不在意。

column1: The knights and guardsmen are too tired to chase your fleeing forms through the brush. They just wave their weapons angrily and rejoin the noble.
column2: 骑士与卫士疲乏不堪，无力追击你等穿林而逃。他们 лишь愤怒挥剑，复归贵族麾下。

column1: The kobold's poetry fails to impress you. But what he says is true. For better or worse, you must hope for a kobold victory. Your best course of action is to seek out and defeat the dwarf lord, $NamedOneName.
column2: 地精之诗未能打动你。然其所言属实。无论成败，唯有寄望地精获胜。汝等最佳之举，便是寻觅并击败矮人之主$NamedOneName。

column1: The kobold's poetry fails to impress you. But what he says is true. For better or worse, you must hope for a kobold victory. Your best course of action is to seek out and defeat the slavemaster, $NamedOneName.
column2: 地精的诗未能打动你。但他所言不虚。无论好坏，你唯有寄望地精获胜。你最好的行动便是寻觅并击败那名奴隶主，$NamedOneName。

column1: The kobolds carry forward small boxes, each containing a precious alchemical potion. Carefully they place the potions at your feet and fade away, still chittering to one another about their great victory. The dwarfs too are gone. You are alone.
column2: 地精们搬运着一个个小匣子，内藏珍贵的炼金药剂。他们小心翼翼地将药剂置于你足下，随即悄然隐去，仍彼此叽叽喳喳地谈论着他们的伟大胜利。矮人亦已离去。你独处一隅。

column1: The kobolds finally force you to yield. They batter you senseless, take all your goods, and drag you back outside the mine.
column2: 地精终于迫使你屈服。他们将你打得不省人事，夺走你所有财物，并把你拖出矿井。

column1: The kobolds finally force you to yield. They batter you senseless, take all your goods, and drag you back outside the mine. When you awaken, you must re-arm with sticks of wood.
column2: 地精终于迫使你屈服。他们将你打得不省人事，夺走所有财物，并把你拖出矿井。待你醒来时，只得重新以木棍武装自己。

column1: The kobolds hand you a glass tube inside of which resides a tiny homunculus. It speaks, in a voice so tiny as to be almost inaudible. "I can predict the future. Each time you ask me a question, the glass becomes thinner. One day, you'll ask me a question too many, the glass will break, and I'll escape to serve you no more. Till then, use me like any other object or tool at your disposal."
column2: 地精递给你一支玻璃管，管中栖息着一个微小的魔偶。它开口说话，声音细若蚊蚋，几不可闻。“我能预知未来。每当你向我提问一次，玻璃便薄一分。终有一日，你问得太多，玻璃碎裂，我将逃离，不再为你效命。在此之前，尽可将我视作寻常器物或工具。”

column1: The lancers stand back, aghast. A feeling of peace and harmony fills the space, while the goblin-steeds grumble in displeasure. When the work of Heaven is done, all warlike feelings are gone. One of the lancers steps forward. "Your saint's pacifism has left us unable to harm you. However, we need not give up the Sword of War. Since we cannot harm you, you must agree to be harmed. If you wish the Sword of War, you must each give us a quart of blood. Will you or no?"
column2: 骑枪手们惊骇地退后。一片宁静与和谐弥漫其间，而地精坐骑却不满地低鸣。当天意已成，一切好战之情尽消。一名骑枪手上前一步。“你的圣者之和平主义使我们无力加害于你。然而，我们无须放弃战争之剑。既然无法伤你，你便须承受伤害。若要此剑，你们每人须献出一夸脱鲜血。可否？”

column1: The last remarks of the defeated Hussites echo in your ears.
column2: 败北的胡斯派最后的话语在你耳畔回响。

column1: The last wolf falls beneath your attack with a howl that sounds almost human. The ear-splitting shriek sends shivers up and down your spine.
column2: 最后一只狼在你的攻击下倒下，发出一声近乎人类的嚎叫。那震耳欲聋的尖啸令你脊背发凉。

column1: The laughter of the city guards echoes from the street and walls behind you.
column2: 城市守卫的笑声从你身后的街道与城墙间回荡。

column1: The lead knob.
column2: 铅制旋钮。

column1: The leader considers the suggestion, then shrugs. "Too much trouble. Let them go!"
column2: 首领思忖片刻，随即耸肩道：“麻烦太多。放他们走吧！”

column1: The leader gives you a dour look. "Time to take your medicine," he says, while the thugs strip you of weapons and armor, as well as a few possessions.
column2: 头目冷冷地看了你一眼。“该让你尝尝苦头了，”他说道，同时打手们剥去你的武器与护甲，以及几件随身物品。

column1: The leader leans back thoughtfully.
column2: 领袖若有所思地向后倚靠。

column1: The leader of the thieves guffaws. "Hah! Easy pickings, my friends!" he cries. They charge you, blades flashing.
column2: 盗贼头目哈哈大笑：“哈！易如反掌，我的朋友们！”他喊道。他们挥舞着刀刃向你冲来。

column1: The leader of the thugs looks you up and down.
column2: 暴徒的头目上下打量着你。

column1: The leader takes your money and laughs.
column2: 首领收下你的钱，放声大笑。

column1: The leader's private chambers are filled with papers, ledgers, and letters. Unfortunately, even $ChosenOneName cannot read fast enough, or well enough, to make sense of this! Worse, you would need three big wagons to carry all the evidence.
column2: 领袖的密室堆满了文书、账簿与信札。可惜，连$ChosenOneName也读得不够快，更谈不上读懂！更糟的是，这些证据若要搬运，需三辆大车方能装下。

column1: The lieutenant is a lifelong resident of $PlaceName, like most of the officers. He sees the wisdom of this advice, and lets the crowd pass.
column2: 中尉是$PlaceName的终身居民，正如大多数军官一样。他深谙此言之理，遂让人群通过。

column1: The lieutenant of the guard accepts your generous donation to the defense of $PlaceName. He calls his men over and splits the money with them while the crowd moves past.
column2: 卫队中尉接受了你对$PlaceName防御的慷慨捐赠。他唤来手下，与他们平分这笔钱，而人群则继续向前移动。

column1: The lieutenant roars at his master, "What? You'd abandon us to save your paltry hide? Die, cur!" Leaping at $NamedOneName, the lieutenant impales his master and dodges out a side door, crying the alert.
column2: 中尉对其主人怒吼道：“什么？你要弃我们而去，只为保全你那卑贱的性命？去死吧，畜生！”中尉跃向$NamedOneName，将主人刺穿，随即闪身逃入侧门，高声示警。

column1: The light in the monk's eyes is feverish as he speaks to you: "Leave me, satanic ones! I invoke the name of the Lord against thee!" Then he falls to the floor in a stupor and speaks no more.
column2: 僧侣眼中闪烁着狂热的光芒，对你说：“走开，你们这些恶魔！我以主之名诅咒你们！”随即他昏倒在地，再无言语。

column1: The local merchants $Support1 change.
column2: 当地商户$Support1更替。

column1: The lord at last states, "You are wise folk, indeed."
column2: 领主终于说道：“你们果然是智者。”

column1: The lord finally says, "Clearly your fame is not due to your skill with weapons."
column2: 领主终于说道：“显然，你的声名并非源于你的武艺。”

column1: The lord finally says, "Such skill is worthy indeed. I am impressed."
column2: 领主终于说道：“如此技艺，确实值得称道。吾甚为钦佩。”

column1: The lord is quiet, but looks at you with respect, tinged with a little superstitious fear. You wonder what $NamedOneName said to the lord to elicit such a response.
column2: 领主沉默不语，却以敬意凝视着你，其中夹杂着些许迷信的畏惧。你不禁思索，$NamedOneName究竟对领主说了些什么，竟能引得他如此反应。

column1: The lord looks at you sadly. "Your accusations hold no sting, for I know them to be false." Then he looks each of you in the eye.
column2: 领主悲戚地望着你。“你的指控毫无分量，因我深知其为虚妄。”随后，他逐一与你们对视。

column1: The lord modestly accepts your praise.
column2: 领主谦逊地接受了你的赞美。

column1: The mad priest $NamedThreeName scoffs at your offer. "Not one of you knows sufficient Latin to serve me in the slightest degree. Go back to your tutors. Now begone!"
column2: 疯癫的祭司$NamedThreeName嗤笑你的提议。“你们中无人通晓拉丁文，不足以侍奉于我。回去找你们的导师吧。现在，滚开！”

column1: The mad priest $NamedThreeName thinks long and hard. Then he says, "I can read your souls and see your fitness. Between you there is knowledge aplenty of Latin and religion. I am honored to have such servants."
column2: 疯狂的牧师$NamedThreeName沉思良久。然后他说：“我能洞悉你们的灵魂，看清你们的资质。你们之中不乏精通拉丁文与宗教之人。能有如此仆从，实乃吾之荣幸。”

column1: The main gate into $PlaceName, $PlaceDesc, is crowded with people and wagons coming to its annual fair. As in other free cities, the $CityLordTitle directs its affairs for the $CityLordName. You expect you will be $PlaceAttitude here. Therefore you...
column2: 进入$PlaceName的正门，$PlaceDesc，挤满了前来参加其年度集市的人群与马车。一如其他自由市，$CityLordTitle为$CityLordName掌管政务。你料想自己将在此地$PlaceAttitude。因此你...

column1: The main gate of $PlaceName, $PlaceDesc, is crowded with people and wagons. It is the annual fair at the capitol of the lands of $CityLordTitle. You expect you will be $PlaceAttitude here. Therefore you...
column2: $PlaceName的正门，$PlaceDesc，人潮涌动，车马喧嚣。这是$CityLordTitle领地首府一年一度的集市。你料想自己将在此处$PlaceAttitude。因此你...

column1: The main street of $PlaceName is crowded with traffic for the fair. You go toward...
column2: $PlaceName的主街因集市而车水马龙。你朝...走去。

column1: The main street of $PlaceName is full of guildsmen, tradesmen, workers, farmers and other commoners, all shouting revolutionary slogans. You suddenly remember that your rebel friends planned to march on $VarString1 today.
column2: $PlaceName的主街上挤满了公会成员、商人、工人、农民及其他平民，皆高呼革命口号。你忽然想起，你的那些反叛朋友今日正计划向$VarString1进军。

column1: The main street of $PlaceName is well patrolled by nervous troops. You go toward...
column2: $PlaceName的主街由紧张的士兵严密巡逻。你朝...走去。

column1: The main topic of conversation remains the recent political disturbances here. Most people say it was just traitors, trying to betray the city to its enemies. Many are too afraid to speak out at all. In any event, the $CityLordTitle survived, and now seems stronger than ever.
column2: 谈话的焦点仍是此地近来的政治动荡。多数人称，不过是些叛徒，欲将城池拱手相让于敌。许多人因惧怕而噤若寒蝉。无论如何，$CityLordTitle安然无恙，如今更显强盛。

column1: The man gives you a packet of dried herbs, a phial of some dark liquid, and a piece of charcoal. "You can draw the pentagrams," he says. "Place one at each corner and befoul it with the tar and charcoal. Understand?"
column2: 那人递给你一包干草药、一小瓶黑色液体和一块木炭。“你可以画出五芒星，”他说，“在每个角落各置一枚，并用焦油与木炭污之。明白吗？”

column1: The man in red beams. "I must confess I was nervous, for you did not look like witches," he says. "But then, neither do we!" and he and his companions laugh. "Come," he says, "we have much to do." You...
column2: 红衣男子面露喜色。“我得承认，我曾有些忐忑，因你等并不似女巫，”他道，“然则，我们亦非如此！”随即便与同伴大笑起来。“来吧，”他说，“尚有许多要事。”你……

column1: The man in the black cap cries, "Unbelievers! Slay them!" and the group rushes you.
column2: 戴黑帽之人喊道：“不信者！杀之！”众人向你扑来。

column1: The man is so taken aback by this casual response that he does not pursue the matter. He says "No, no," and hurries away.
column2: 那人对这等漫不经心的回应大为惊愕，竟未再追问。他连声道“不，不”，便匆匆离去。

column1: The man leans back and smiles peacefully. "Bless you for your aid," he says. "In return, listen carefully: in the upper reaches of the tower there is a deadly trap. Avoid it by twisting the horns of the stag. The stag ..." He falls unconscious, the smile still on his face.
column2: 那人向后倚靠，面带安详的微笑。“感谢你的援手，”他说，“作为回报，请仔细听：塔楼的上层设有一处致命陷阱。绕过它的方法是扭动雄鹿的双角。那头雄鹿……”他随即昏厥，脸上仍挂着微笑。

column1: The man nods. "Ah yes, I had heard that," he says, retiring once again to his hiding place. You get the feeling that he was only testing you.
column2: 那人点头道：“啊，是的，我确曾听闻此事。”随即又退回藏身之处。你隐约觉得，他不过是在试探你罢了。

column1: The man who comes to the door is odd-looking indeed, made more so by having been awakened. His eyes pop out of his head in an expression of perpetual surprise, and his hair is a wild nest. He smiles and invites you in.
column2: 来开门的那人相貌奇特，更因被惊醒而显得怪异。他双眼圆睁，似永远处于惊诧之中，头发如乱巢般蓬松。他微笑着邀你入内。

column1: The man's voice is thin and hard. "I thought as much," he says. "You are not the Schulz, and these are not your witches!" He barks then, like a wolf, and the lupine sentries spring to the attack!
column2: 那人的声音尖细而冷硬。“我早料到如此，”他说，“你不是舒尔茨，这些也不是你的女巫！”他随即如狼般嚎叫，那些狼形的哨兵便扑将上来！

column1: The mask of Krott says, "To pass, tell me if I be a dwarf, kobold or gnone."
column2: 克罗特的面具说道：“欲通行，须答我乃矮人、地精，抑或无名之物。”

column1: The master huntsman who leads them asserts, "This is my lord's demesne. Leave or pay rent: $Money2 per week."
column2: 领队的猎户长宣称：“此乃吾主之领地。离去或缴租：每周$Money2。”

column1: The master immediately disappears into the office, while the guards hustle you out.
column2: 主人随即隐入内室，卫士则匆匆将你驱出。

column1: The master of the bank steps out of the rear offices, and stands among his clerks and guards.
column2: 银行主人自后堂而出，立于其账房与卫士之间。

column1: The masters sneer at the idea that any of their members would be interested in providing tutoring or training to outsiders such as yourself.
column2: 主人们嗤之以鼻，认为他们中的任何一员都不会对像你这样的外人施以教导或训练。

column1: The mercenaries fall in beside the front ranks of the crowd. To your practiced eye, they don't look any more reliable than the citizens themselves!
column2: 佣兵们排在人群的前排。在你练就的眼中，他们看起来并不比市民更可靠！

column1: The mine of $PlaceName is a cluster of shacks. Despite the squalid look, miners are highly skilled professionals. They live here only when hard at work, not year-round. But no work is going on now. About twenty miners come out and look at you. One steps over to talk.
column2: $PlaceName的矿井是一片棚屋聚集地。尽管外表破败，矿工们却是技艺高超的专业人士。他们只在劳作时才在此居住，并非终年不离。然而此刻并无工作进行。约有二十名矿工走出，打量着你。其中一人走上前来交谈。

column1: The miner continues, "Some said the knockers rapped at the walls to warn us of cave-ins or coal gas. Others said they rapped to tempt us into danger. Perhaps they did both, at different times. But we always left bread, milk, and beer for them. We wanted no trouble.
column2: 矿工继续说道：“有人说敲击声是在提醒我们有塌方或瓦斯。也有人说那是诱我们入险。或许两者皆有，只是时机不同。但我们总要留些面包、牛奶和啤酒给他们，免生事端。”

column1: The miners issue forth from their huts. They amble glumly toward you. The defeat in your eyes tells them everything they need to know. One of them tries to cheer you up. "Not even Charlemagne's knights could have cleared out that mine. Dwarf cunning and dwarf magic and dwarf traps are too much for human ingenuity. It's not your fault."
column2: 矿工们从茅屋中走出，闷闷地朝你走来。你眼中的挫败已道尽一切。其中一人试图安慰你：“连查理曼大帝的骑士也未必能清理那矿坑。矮人的狡智、矮人的魔法与矮人的陷阱，远非人力所能及。这并非你的过错。”

column1: The mist is impossible to ignore. Your vision fades as your eyes seem to burn away. Your hacking coughs turn to blood as the mist destroys your lungs. Frantically you search.
column2: 雾气令人无法忽视。视线渐失，双眼仿佛被灼烧。咳嗽带血，雾气已毁肺腑。你慌乱地四下搜寻。

column1: The mob roars and you are trampled by a human wave that surges over you to the guardsmen. They fling down their weapons. The rebel leaders are freed and hoisted onto triumphant shoulders. As the people celebrate, you quietly crawl away down an alleyway.
column2: 暴民怒吼，人潮涌向卫兵，将你踩踏于地。卫兵弃械，叛首获释，被高举于众肩之上。众人欢庆之际，你悄然沿小巷爬离。

column1: The monastery is almost completely dark. You know the monks won't do anything for you tonight, so you decide to...
column2: 修道院几乎一片漆黑。你知今夜僧侣不会相助，遂决定……

column1: The monastery's abbot refuses to let you near the books. "We are not so cloistered that we have not had word of you. Not everything we hear makes us convinced that our precious books would be in good hands."
column2: 修道院院长拒你近书。“虽处幽闭，然耳闻汝名。所闻之事，并未令吾等确信珍籍可托。”

column1: The monk has a sad expression on his face. "You are importunate, but then, these are hard times. I will do as you ask."
column2: 僧侣面露忧色：“汝虽执拗，然时局艰难。吾当依汝所请。”

column1: The monk nods back with a sad smile and watches you depart. Soon the shrine disappears behind you.
column2: 僧侣含悲微笑，目送你离去。不久，圣坛便隐于身后。

column1: The monk says he will take your request to the abbot. In minutes he returns, saying, "Kind sirs, the abbot says that the task remains undone. He has nothing more to say until it is completed."
column2: 僧侣称将转呈院长。须臾归来，言：“诸位善士，院长云任务未竟，未完之前无话可说。”

column1: The monk seems reluctant to speak with you. His body twitches involuntarily and he avoids your gaze. He mumbles disjointedly, "There is only one thing I need ... never tell secret ... God give me strength ..." You...
column2: 僧侣似不愿与你交谈。身体不自主抽搐，避而不视。喃喃道：“吾唯需一事……切莫泄露秘密……愿上帝赐我力量……”你……

column1: The monk shrugs and says, "I am sorry. We waited long for you, and nothing was accomplished. Then others, quite virtuously, fulfilled our needs. We rewarded them justly."
column2: 僧侣耸肩道：“抱歉。久候汝至，终无所成。后有他人，以义举解吾困，吾已厚酬之。”

column1: The monks accept your money with dignity and promise to add prayers for you in their next Mass, which starts soon. They seat you in a cloistered room rather than offering to let you join in.
column2: 僧侣庄重收钱，允于下次弥撒为你祈福，弥撒即刻开始。他们引你入静室，而非邀你共礼。

column1: The monks silently bow, while the farmers nod politely. You can't tell if they are naturally reticent, afraid of strangers bearing arms and armor, or worried about something else. Whatever it is, you can learn nothing from them.
column2: 僧侣默然致意，农夫礼貌颔首。不知其天性寡言，抑或惧携甲胄之人，抑或另有顾虑。无论如何，你难从中探得消息。

column1: The monks smile, but return to work. You realize they must be under a vow of silence. The peasant farmers will talk, but only about the prospects for rain, last year's crop, and other trivia. At least everyone seems happy and content here.
column2: 僧侣微笑，复归工作。你悟其必守缄默之誓。农夫则谈雨情、去年收成及其他琐事。至少此间人人安乐自足。

column1: The monster gives you a perfectly formed miniature sword, no more than a finger's length. $ChosenOneName stops bleeding, but all attempts at bandaging $his injuries fail. $He will never be the same. You return to the courtyard.
column2: 怪物赠汝一柄指长之微型宝剑。$ChosenOneName止血，然包扎你的伤势皆无效。你再难如初。汝归庭院。

column1: The monster gives you a perfectly-formed miniature sword, a finger's length. You stop bleeding after a time, but all attempts at bandaging your injuries fail. You will never be the same. You return to the courtyard with your dearly-bought prize.
column2: 怪物赠汝一柄指长之微型宝剑。经时止血，然包扎无效。汝再难如初。携此贵重之物，归于庭院。

column1: The monsters appear satisfied and move off. Shakily, you stagger away from this terribe place.
column2: 怪物满意而去。汝踉跄离此险地。

column1: The monsters step forward with appalling speed and quickly slash your arms, catching the blood in their helmets. After you have given up the requisite quart, you are allowed to bandage your wounds. The largest lancer says ominously, "This blood is ours. You shall be weaker forever."
column2: 怪物疾步上前，迅斩汝臂，以头盔接血。献出所需一夸脱后，始许包扎。最大之枪手阴沉道：“此血乃吾所有，汝将永弱。”

column1: The monstrous apocalypse dragon cackles hatefully as you run away. Perhaps you should return after better-preparing yourselves for this difficult combat.
column2: 怪异末日巨龙见汝逃遁，狂笑不已。或许汝应更周密准备，再战于此。

column1: The monstrous head speaks, "I can now, should I choose, unleash the last plague upon the world, which shall destroy all. However, the time is not yet perfectly ripe. I would rather not yet accomplish the fullness of my design. Hence, I offer you a choice -- a gamble. You may choose to receive my gift, or continue to doom.
column2: 怪物之首言：“吾今若欲，可降末劫于世，毁灭万物。然时机未至，吾尚不愿全盘实现夙愿。故予汝一选——一场豪赌。汝可受吾馈，亦可任命运摆布。”

column1: The moonlight filters down through a quiet stand of trees. Amid the shadows, you decide to...
column2: 月光透过静谧林木洒落。阴影之中，汝决……

column1: The most interesting news right now is how Frau Glinker's cat got into the $cityChurch's baptismal font last Sunday! The sight of the poor censor chasing the animal up and down still provokes gales of laughter.
column2: 当前最趣闻，乃格林克夫人之猫上周日闯入$cityChurch洗礼池！可怜的监察官追猫上下之状，至今仍引哄堂大笑。

column1: The most repulsive hag howls and leaps upon you. The rest follow a second later. You have no choice but to fight back.
column2: 最丑陋之女巫嚎叫扑上，其余紧随其后。汝唯有奋起反击。

column1: The mumbled words of prayer appear to make the guards uneasy. The leader of the knights constantly glances at the east door, with a look that speaks volumes: "What if their prayers reveal the location of the secret door?" Even its operation is evident, merely from the way he moves his body.
column2: 吟诵之声似令卫兵不安。骑士首领频频望东门，神色意味深长：“若祷告泄露密门所在，如何？”仅凭其举止，便可窥其心思。

column1: The mystery of the cave hovers in the back of your minds as you decide to pass up this adventure and continue your travels.
column2: 洞穴之谜萦绕心头，汝遂决定放弃此历险，续行旅程。

column1: The next day a runner brings word from the city gates.
column2: 次日，信使自城门传来消息。

column1: The next day you search for those left behind. You find them a short distance from the battle site, left for dead.
column2: 次日，汝寻觅遗落之人。于战场不远处发现，奄奄一息。

column1: The next day you search for those left behind. You find them a short distance from the battle site, left for dead. Alas, the kidnappers and $ChosenOneName are long gone. You keenly feel a sense of failure.
column2: 次日，汝寻觅遗落之人。于战场不远处发现，奄奄一息。惜绑匪与$ChosenOneName早已遁去。汝深感失败。

column1: The next day you seek the friends you left behind. You find them a short distance from the battlefield, stripped and left for dead.
column2: 次日，汝寻昔日友伴。于战场附近发现，衣衫尽脱，命悬一线。

column1: The next day, an emissary comes from the abbot and orders the turnkey to free you, saying, "You are hereby released into the custody of the Church." The emissary walks with you out of the jail, and escorts you to the city church. There, he states, "As a friend of the Church, you are to be freed. We are not sure we can rescue you again should you be arrested, so be careful."
column2: 次日，院长遣使至，命狱卒放汝，曰：“兹释放汝，交由教会看管。”使者陪汝出狱，护送至城中教堂，谓：“汝乃教会之友，特予释放。若再被捕，恐难相救，务慎之。”

column1: The next morning $ChosenOneName relates $his experiences to the group. You all realize that the founding virtues of this place have been quite forgotten. Such things are not unknown; but it is disconcerting to encounter it personally! You also resolve to remember the place named. It could be important.
column2: 次晨，$ChosenOneName向众人述你的经历。汝等皆觉此地立身之本已湮没。此类事非无闻，然亲历仍令人不安！汝等亦决心铭记此地之名，或有大用。

column1: The night watch cries out in alarm as the potion explodes. Meanwhile, you dash down a side alley, making a quick escape. However, just to be sure, you circle around to a distant side street.
column2: 夜巡惊呼，药剂骤爆。汝则奔入侧巷，急遽脱身。然为稳妥，绕至远街。

column1: The night watch leans out of the tower and shines the lantern upon you.
column2: 夜巡探身塔楼，以灯照汝。

column1: The night watch spreads out, trying to surround you, while their leader steps forward, demanding, "Who violates the curfew of $PlaceName?"
column2: 夜巡四散围汝，首领上前，厉声道：“何人违$PlaceName宵禁？”

column1: The night watch strips you of weapons, armor, and everything else of obvious value. They bind you securely and drag you off to the prison cells of the Dungeon.
column2: 夜巡夺汝武器、甲胄及一切值物，缚汝押入地牢囚室。

column1: The night watchman shines his lantern upon you.
column2: 夜巡以灯照汝。

column1: The nobleman laughs in your face. "Miserable wretches with petty arguments! Why should I listen to such drivel?" He gestures impatiently to his men, "Have them pay, immediately!"
column2: 贵族嗤笑于汝：“区区琐事，尔等穷酸之辈！吾何须听汝胡言？”他不耐挥手下令，“速付罚金！”

column1: The noise of your battle has certainly alerted other denizens of this area, though none appear to be coming at this moment.
column2: 汝之战响已惊动此地居民，然暂无人现身。

column1: The normally conservative Jewelers' guild $VarPhrase1 changes in the city government.
column2: 向来保守之珠宝商行$VarPhrase1于市政变革中易主。

column1: The noted merchant families of $PlaceName $VarPhrase5 change in the city.
column2: $PlaceName著名商贾家族$VarPhrase5于市政更迭中易主。

column1: The novice gently escorts you from the tower, and asks, "What is your pleasure now?"
column2: 新人轻步陪汝下塔，问：“今欲何为？”

column1: The nuns hesitate, then one elderly woman speaks forth boldly. "I'm sorry, but we have not enough beds for honest men and women, let alone folk such as you."
column2: 修女迟疑，老妪毅然发声：“抱歉，吾等床位不足，岂堪容纳正直男女？更遑论汝等。”

column1: The obvious reply is for you to open up the magic lantern, which dispels the gloom at once. Baphomet is once more defeated, but still chants his litany, "Though you cure the darkness it matters not, for there are three plagues yet to come, and they each are worse than the first four put together!"
column2: 明显之策，乃启魔灯，顷刻驱散黑暗。巴佛墨特再度败北，犹念咒曰：“纵汝驱暗，亦无济于事，尚有三劫未至，且每劫皆胜前四劫之总合！”

column1: The officer gives you a considering stare.
column2: 军官凝视汝良久。

column1: The officer walks around you slowly.
column2: 军官缓步绕汝一周。

column1: The old librarian nods and talks happily about the documents they have concerning various saints. You discuss your preferences, and discover that today you only have time to study one saint, and only one person can see the sources at a time.
column2: 老馆长点头，欣谈诸圣典籍。汝等商议偏好，终定今日仅研一圣，且每次仅一人可阅原典。

column1: The old man bows and leaves. You all do likewise.
column2: 老者鞠躬辞去，汝等亦随之。

column1: The old man is no match for your powerful weapons; he quickly succumbs to your attack. Was he an enemy, waiting to spring a trap? You'll never know for certain, but how could there be a friend here?
column2: 老者非汝强兵之敌，瞬即毙命。彼果为伏敌否？汝终不得而知，然此地岂有友乎？

column1: The old monk clears his throat and asks if you have other requests. You...
column2: 老僧清了清嗓子，问你是否还有其他请求。你...

column1: The old monk promises to inquire and bids you wait for an answer. You take seats on a wooden bench and wait.
column2: 老僧答应去打听，并让你稍候等候答复。你便在木凳上坐下，静待消息。

column1: The old monk returns, smiling.
column2: 老僧笑吟吟地回来了。

column1: The old woman speaks, "They say that metal will soon be in short supply. The mines have stopped producing. One miner who came through the village said there was a curse. You should ask the miners, they would know more."
column2: 老妪开口道：“听说金属即将告罄。矿井已停采。有位过村的矿工说，此地遭了诅咒。你不妨去问问那些矿工，他们或许更知详情。”

column1: The old, wealthy burgher families $VarPhrase1 change in the city government
column2: $VarPhrase1古老富庶市民家族于市政变革中易主。

column1: The ongoing feud in the countryside is nothing but a nuisance to the people here.
column2: 乡间的纷争不过是此间百姓的烦扰罢了。

column1: The ongoing war doesn't seem to worry people. The popular view is, "Well, one noble or another will win. Our walls are so strong, no siege will ever succeed. They'll settle it somewhere else, with armies."
column2: 持续的战事似乎并未令众人忧虑。时人多言：“无非此家胜彼家而已。我城坚壁固，何敌能破？胜负自有他人定夺，战场自会移往他处。”

column1: The only break in the monotony of the stone walls is a large, heavy, locked door in the south wall, and some sort of plaque on the north wall. You ...
column2: 石墙间唯一的异景，乃南墙上一扇沉重的锁门，北墙上则有一块铭牌。你……

column1: The only break in the monotony of the stone walls is a large, heavy, locked door in the south wall, and some sort of plaque on the north wall. You...
column2: 石墙间唯一的异景，乃南墙上一扇沉重的锁门，北墙上则有一块铭牌。你……

column1: The only bright spot is the $McGuffin, resting peacefully atop one of the graves!
column2: 唯一的亮色，便是那静静安卧于墓顶之上的$McGuffin！

column1: The only signs of the tower keep against the cloudy sky are the occasional gleams at the windows. Meanwhile you decide to...
column2: 高塔在阴云下仅余窗间偶露的微光。与此同时，你决定……

column1: The other, though he may call himself a witch, is really just a common man, and most men are afraid of the supernatural, especially in the company of strangers. He backs away.
column2: 另一人虽自称术士，实则凡夫俗子耳。凡人皆畏鬼神，尤惧陌路之妖邪。他遂退避三舍。

column1: The parcel appears, and the $NamedTwoName is unwrapped and presented to you.
column2: 包裹现身，$NamedTwoName被拆开，呈于汝前。

column1: The party slowly continues down the tunnel, expecting danger at every step.  The torchlight casts its dim light on the rock floor, revealing nothing unusual, until the shape of an old storage chest appears out of the gloom. The party is hurrying forward to examine it when a bear charges out of a previously unseen side tunnel! You fall back to...
column2: 队伍缓步前行，步步惊心。火把映照岩地，未见异状，忽见一旧木箱隐现于暗影之中。众人欲上前细察，忽有巨熊自侧洞扑出！汝等退至……

column1: The pass into Switzerland is blocked for now; you must turn back. You hope that sometime in the future this route will be open.
column2: 通往瑞士之路暂且阻绝，汝只得折返。愿他日此途重开。

column1: The path is blocked by a dark iron door. Carved over it are some numbers:
column2: 小径为一道黝黑铁门所阻。其上镌刻着若干数字：

column1: The path is blocked by a grim iron door. Carved on it are some letters, as follows:
column2: 小径为一道森然铁门所阻。门上镌刻着如下文字：

column1: The path is blocked by a grim iron door. Carved over it is the legend:
column2: 小径为一道森然铁门所阻。门楣镌刻着如下铭文：

column1: The path is blocked by a grim iron door. To one side is a golden statue of a dwarf. On the other is a silver statue of a dwarf. Embossed on the door are the words:
column2: 小径为一道森然铁门所阻。一侧立一尊金矮人像，另一侧立一银矮人像。门上浮雕着如下字样：

column1: The path is blocked by a heavy door. Carved over it is the legend:
column2: 小径为一道厚重之门所阻。门楣镌刻着如下铭文：

column1: The path is blocked by a heavy door. Carved overhead are the words:
column2: 小径为一道厚重之门所阻。门上方镌刻着如下文字：

column2: 小径为一道厚重铁门所阻。门上方镌刻着如下文字：

column1: The path is blocked by a heavy, iron door. Above the door is carved:
column2: 小径为一道厚重铁门所阻。门上方镌刻着：

column1: The path is blocked by an heavy iron door. Carved above it is an inscription:
column2: 小径为一道厚重铁门所阻。门上方镌刻着一则铭文：

column2: 小径为一道铁门所阻。门上方镌刻着：
